summary:
I reviewed `git diff origin/mockup...HEAD` on feature/anatomy-atlas-3d without modifying any file. ESLint on the viewer, page, logic and client exits clean, and so does `corepack yarn tsc -p tsconfig.app.json --noEmit`.

What holds up: SSR keeps the viewer inert. The page returns early when not in a browser, three.js is loaded with `import()` inside `afterNextRender`, and the committed initial-bundle tables for base and branch match (1.36 MB). Colours are read from tokens at runtime, and reduced motion turns off damping. Most listeners are removed in `liberar()`.

Why it fails:
1. **Wrong piece list (major).** The viewer is projected inside `<app-view-state-host>`. Angular creates projected components even while the host is showing its skeleton, so the viewer starts while `parts` is still `[]`. It copies `parts()` once and never updates it, so if three.js loads before `parts.json`, every mesh stays hidden for good.
2. **GPU resources after leaving the page (major).** If you navigate away while a GLB is downloading, the download still finishes after `liberar()` and adds meshes and draws to a renderer that was already disposed. The WebGL context is also never released.
3. **Related pieces blend in (major).** In dark mode the "related" highlight is the same colour as the Nervous layer, and in light mode three of the colours are close shades of amber.
4. **No browser evidence (major).** No screenshots are committed for the new templates.

There are also smaller issues with state, accessibility and tests (see the minor findings). Per the review rules, I cannot approve while issues of HIGH severity are present.

findings.title: The viewer is created while `parts` is still `[]` and copies it once, so the model can stay invisible
findings.evidence: In glossary-anatomy-atlas.html:43-53, <app-anatomy-viewer> is projected content of <app-view-state-host [state]="partsState()">. ViewStateHost only renders the default <ng-content /> in its @default branch (view-state-host.html:195), but Angular instantiates projected components no matter which branch is showing. So the viewer is constructed during S2 with [parts]="parts()" === [] (page .ts:130). `afterNextRender` then runs `arrancar()` on a detached canvas. Motor builds `partePorMalla` once from `this.parts()` (line 140 -> line 215). The effect at lines 106-112 does not track `parts()`, and Motor has no way to receive new parts. If the three/OrbitControls/GLTFLoader chunks resolve before catalog/parts.json (156 KB), every mesh hits `parte === undefined -> malla.visible = false` (lines 301-304) for good, and picking returns nothing. In the error state the hidden viewer still downloads three.js and the default GLBs (skeleton.glb 885 KB, organs.glb 295 KB) for nothing. The Playwright spec only passes when the race goes the right way.
findings.fix: Create the viewer only once data is ready, for example `@if (partsState().status === 'ready')` outside the host or a dedicated template slot, or make Motor react to `parts` by tracking it in the effect and rebuilding `partePorMalla` before calling `pintar()`. Add a test that sets `parts` after the viewer has started.

findings.title: After destroy, a layer still loading keeps adding meshes, drawing and updating state; the WebGL context is never released
findings.evidence: `liberar()` (lines 444-461) disposes the meshes in `this.mallas` and the renderer, but it sets no flag and does not cancel loads already in flight. When a pending `cargador.loadAsync(...).then` resolves, it still runs `this.mallas.set`, `this.escena.add` and `encuadrar()` (lines 267-280). `encuadrar()` calls `pedirDibujo()`, which schedules a new rAF -> `renderer.render` on the disposed renderer. `aplicar`'s `.then` calls `alCargar('ready')`, which runs `status.set` and `statusChange.emit` on the destroyed component. Angular 21.2.18 logs NG0953 "Unexpected emit for destroyed OutputRef" (checked in @angular/core fesm2022/_resource-chunk.mjs:40). The geometries and materials of those late meshes are never disposed. The materials the GLTF brings, replaced at line 272, are never disposed either. Nothing calls `renderer.forceContextLoss()`, so repeated visits to the route pile up WebGL contexts until GC, and Chromium caps them at about 16.
findings.fix: Add a `liberado` flag in Motor. Check it at the start of the `cargarCapa`/`aplicar` callbacks, and when set, dispose the incoming gltf.scene instead of adding it. In `liberar()`, also dispose the replaced materials and call `renderer.forceContextLoss()`.

findings.title: In dark mode the related highlight is the same colour as the Nervous layer; in light mode three layer/highlight colours are close shades of amber
findings.evidence: Mapping: skeleton `--c-amber-300`, nervous `--c-warning-400` (= `var(--c-amber-400)`, styles.css:75), related `--brand-accent`. `--brand-accent` is `var(--c-amber-500)` in light (styles.css:216) and `var(--c-amber-400)` in dark (styles.css:288 and 337). So in dark mode a related piece is exactly the same colour as any nervous-system piece, and the page's 'Relacionadas' highlight cannot be told apart once that layer is on. In light mode skeleton, nervous and related are amber 300/400/500, and organs (`petrol-300`) is close to the selected colour (`--brand-primary` = petrol-500). The difference relies on hue alone, which also fails WCAG 1.4.1. The Playwright spec only checks that a sheet opens and never checks the highlight.
findings.fix: Use highlight colours that are far from every layer colour in both themes (preferably dedicated semantic tokens for the atlas), and do not rely on colour alone. The emissive/dimming already helps, but the selected and related colours must not equal a layer colour.

findings.title: No browser evidence for the new templates (NO_EVIDENCE_NO_DONE)
findings.evidence: The spec writes screenshots to docs/progress/evidence/anatomy-atlas/screenshots/. That directory exists but is empty, and `git ls-files docs/progress/evidence/anatomy-atlas` lists only the two build/initial-bundle-*.txt files. The path is not gitignored (`git check-ignore` gives no output). Unit tests cover the viewer only in its 'unsupported' state (anatomy-viewer.spec.ts), so the 462-line Motor, the keyboard handling, picking and highlighting have no committed evidence that they render. tsc and eslint pass, but they do not check templates.
findings.fix: Run `yarn pw --workers=1 atlas-anatomico-3d` and commit the screenshots and the run output (375/768/1440 light, 1440 dark, Male/Female), or state explicitly that it was not run.

findings.title: The load status can show 'ready' while another layer is still loading, and a later success hides an earlier error
findings.evidence: Each `aplicar` waits only for its own missing layers (`faltan`). Turn on Muscles (2.3 MB), then Nervous (417 KB): the second call has faltan=['nervous'] and sets 'ready' while muscles.glb is still downloading. Likewise, if one layer fails ('error') and another then succeeds, the success sets 'ready' and the role=alert message telling the user to retry disappears.
findings.fix: Work out the status from the set of pending/failed promises in `capasCargadas` (loading if any are pending, error if any of the requested layers failed) instead of from each `Promise.all` separately.

findings.title: A focusable canvas with keyboard interaction uses role="img", a non-interactive role
findings.evidence: `tabindex="0" role="img"` plus a `(keydown)` handler that takes over the arrow keys. With role=img, screen readers in browse mode keep the arrow keys for themselves and never pass them to the canvas, so the rotation described in the aria-label is unreachable for them. The 'Cargando…' status (line 14) is inserted together with its text in the same render, so it is often not announced.
findings.fix: Use role="application" with aria-roledescription="modelo 3D" (or a group with instructions in aria-describedby), and keep a live region in the DOM at all times whose text changes.

findings.title: A selected piece in a hidden layer dims the whole model and leaves nothing highlighted
findings.evidence: `hayFoco = elegidas.size > 0` does not check whether the selected meshes are visible. Search for 'femur' with the Skeleton layer off: every visible mesh drops to 0.16 opacity and the femur is hidden (its layer is not in `capas`). The visibility rule from line 308 also repeats `partVisibleFor` from glossary-anatomy-atlas.logic.ts:37.
findings.fix: Count focus only when selected meshes are visible, or turn the selected piece's layer on when it is opened from search.

findings.title: Nested <main> inside the shell's main landmark
findings.evidence: The page wraps its content in `<main class="atlas3d">`, but the route renders inside ShellLayout, which already has `<main class="app-main__inner" id="contenido-principal">` (shell-layout.html:672). That creates two main landmarks, one inside the other, which is invalid HTML. glossary-network.html:7 already does the same, but this change adds another instance.
findings.fix: Use a <div> or <section> as the page root.

findings.title: Right-click or pinch with little movement counts as a pick
findings.evidence: `alBajar`/`alSoltar` do not filter by `button` or by number of active pointers. Right-click (OrbitControls' pan) or a two-finger pinch released with less than 5 px of movement fires `alElegir`, and the page then changes or clears the `structure` query param.
findings.fix: Ignore `evento.button !== 0` and gestures with more than one active pointer.

findings.title: Netter 'Riñón' (kidney) left unmapped although the human subset has the exact kidney class
findings.evidence: ENT_b325b9c12845dd 'Riñón' queries ['kidney'], uberon null, reason 'sin coincidencia exacta en UBERON'. In uberon.obo 2026-10-01, UBERON:0002113 'kidney' has no FMA xref, so the human filter drops it (tools/anatomy-atlas-3d/extract_ontology.py:192 keeps a term only when t['fma'] is non-empty). FMA:7203 (Kidney) sits on UBERON:0000082 'adult mammalian kidney', which is in uberon-human.json (fma ['7203']) and in public catalog index.json as 'riñón de mamífero adulto'. `uberon_lookup.py "adult mammalian kidney"` returns UBERON:0000082 via label. So one of the main organs in the atlas has no Netter link.
findings.fix: Map ENT_b325b9c12845dd to UBERON:0000082 (query 'adult mammalian kidney'). For the other unmapped organ-level entries, also try the UBERON class that carries the FMA xref.

findings.title: All four Netter renal segmental arteries missed because the queries used the wrong word order
findings.evidence: Sampled ENT_cf621767b947dc 'Arteria(s) — segmentaria — inferior' (plate 335, the intrarenal arteries plate, next to 'Arteria(s) — renales' and 'capsular') was queried as 'inferior segmental artery' / 'inferior segmental artery of kidney' and returned nothing. `uberon_lookup.py --fuzzy` shows the subset has 'inferior segmental renal artery' (UBERON:8920008), 'superior segmental renal artery', 'posterior segmental renal artery' and 'anterior inferior segmental renal artery'. The siblings ENT_d3a0cd878e69c0 (line 799), ENT_71c2cc98de1624 and ENT_04e63e54aa4647 are unmapped the same way.
findings.fix: Re-query using the 'X segmental renal artery' labels and map the four entries.

findings.title: The FMA-xref 'human' criterion drops real human classes, so some exact matches cannot be found
findings.evidence: Non-obsolete UBERON classes with no FMA xref are excluded: kidney (UBERON:0002113), pharynx (UBERON:0001042 label 'chordate pharynx' survives but 'pharynx' does not resolve), eye, and liver serosa (UBERON:8400021, exact synonym 'serosa of liver'). Sampled ENT_3a6bc34fb2490e 'Hígado — peritoneo visceral' (R04.json:3334) queried 'serosa of liver', which is an EXACT synonym of UBERON:8400021 in the OBO, but it came back unmapped because that class is not in uberon-human.json.
findings.fix: Document this as a known limitation in data/anatomy-ontology/README.md, or widen the criterion (for example, the FMA xref OR an in_taxon that covers Homo sapiens) and re-run the lookup for the unmapped entries.

summary:
I checked a sample of 159 Netter entries (seed 20261024): 41 of 805 accepted mappings and 118 of 2356 unmapped entries. False positives: 0 of 41. Missed exact matches: 2 of 118 (Riñón and the inferior renal segmental artery). A third miss (liver serosa) only exists outside the 6074-term subset and is blocked by the subset rule. Nothing outside the sample was audited except the three siblings of the renal-artery miss. Unmapped reasons were checked by re-running uberon_lookup.py (exact and --fuzzy) and grepping the full uberon.obo for the main candidates (linea aspera, lingula of mandible, iliofemoral, acromioclavicular, uterosacral, soleal line, pectineal line, sublingual fossa, cribriform fascia, pararectal fossa, superior mesenteric lymph node, suprahyoid artery, etc.). None of them exist as exact human classes. Where a match exists but the entry is ambiguous (fascia lata, tarsal gland, ascending pharyngeal artery, internal carotid nerve plexus, flexor digitorum brevis), staying unmapped is the right call.

findings.title: Netter (Elsevier) index text and plate numbers are shipped publicly and shown in the UI, including scraped running-header text from the book
findings.evidence: The template has an «En el índice de Netter» block that renders `entrada.name — lámina(s) entrada.plates` (lines 163-175). The data comes from data/netter-anatomia/entities.json. Its manifest.json says primarySource is 'Frank H. Netter, MD. Atlas de Anatomía Humana. 4.ª edición. Elsevier/Masson', taken from a scanned PDF index. The generator (scripts/gen-anatomy-ontology-fixture.mjs:158-160) copies `name` and `plates` into the public catalog: `grep -o '"netterId"' -r public/anatomy-atlas-3d/catalog | wc -l` returns 805. Some of those names are OCR fragments of the book's page header, for example `structures-24.json: "name":"Atlas de anatomía hur — nervio pudendo"` and `structures-01.json: "Atlas de anatomia hum — maxilar"` (8 in public/, 125 in data/anatomy-ontology/netter-mapping/*.json). netter-mapping/*.json (3161 names) and netter-mapping-report.json are new files that carry this Elsevier-derived index text. The credits footer lists only BodyParts3D, UBERON and FMA, and nothing in DISCOVERY.md records a rights check for Netter. This breaks the requirement that no Netter or Elsevier text appear in the new files.
findings.fix: Remove the Netter `name` and `plates` from the public catalog and the UI, or reduce them to an opaque internal ID that is never rendered. Do not commit index strings copied from the book into data/anatomy-ontology/. At minimum, drop the OCR header fragments and record a rights decision for Netter in DISCOVERY.

findings.title: Machine-translated Spanish names are shown in many places without the 'traducción automática sin revisar' label
findings.evidence: `displayName()` returns `labelEs ?? labelEn ?? id`, so the machine translation is preferred everywhere (labelsEs covers 6074 structures, per ATLAS_3D_META). It is used unlabelled in five places: the card title h2 (html:90), search results (html:74), related-structure labels (logic.ts:92 and 101, rendered at html:188 and 190), the female-structures list (html:247), and the viewer aria-label (ts:173). Only the 'Nombre en castellano' row (html:107) and the Spanish definition (html:145-147) carry the label. data/anatomy-ontology/README.md says 'la pantalla la rotula así', which holds only for those two spots.
findings.fix: Mark the MT label wherever labelEs is rendered: a visible badge or suffix on the h2, and one page-level notice next to search, relations and lists. Alternatively, show labelEn as the primary name with the MT as secondary, labelled text.

findings.title: The 'Mujer' list of female structures leaves out the uterus, cervix, myometrium, endometrium and other core female structures
findings.evidence: `femeninas` holds only classes that reach UBERON:0000474 (female reproductive system) through is_a or part_of. In the catalog, uterus UBERON:0000995 is part_of UBERON:0004175 'internal genitalia', which is sex-neutral, so it is never reached. A check of ATLAS_3D_FEMALE_ONLY_IDS against the catalog found 'uterus', 'uterine cervix', 'myometrium', 'body of uterus', 'uterine wall', 'endocervix', 'ectocervix', 'broad ligament of uterus', 'uterine artery', 'vaginal artery' and 'ovarian artery' missing, although 'vaginal vein' and 'placenta' are listed. The aviso (html:37) and DISCOVERY.md:56 both say the view lists 'las 93 estructuras femeninas del catálogo'. Users of the Mujer view therefore get an incomplete female list and no uterus.
findings.fix: Also seed the female set with the uterus (UBERON:0000995) and its part_of closure, or use a curated root list. Add a spec asserting that the uterus and cervix are in ATLAS_3D_FEMALE_ONLY_IDS.

findings.title: DISCOVERY says the BodyParts3D credit comes from a raw file that actually contains a different credit
findings.evidence: DISCOVERY.md:28-30 attributes «BodyParts3D, (c) The Database Center for Life Science licensed under CC Attribution-Share Alike 2.1 Japan» to `bodyparts3d-LICENSE_content.txt`. That file's credit line is different: 'BodyParts3D, Copyrightc 2008 Life Science Integrated Database Center licensed by CC Display-Inheritance 2.1 Japan'. The shipped wording appears verbatim only on line 4 of the README in the BodyParts3D copy (`git -C dl/bp3d show HEAD:README.md`), and that README line was not saved as raw evidence. The shipped credit is defensible, but the evidence chain is broken, and the year '2008' from the license text is dropped everywhere: provenance.json, LICENSE.txt, the GLB asset.copyright and the UI.
findings.fix: Save the README excerpt (line 4) as raw evidence and cite it. Alternatively, state that both credit forms exist and record why the README form was chosen.

findings.title: DISCOVERY points to a REPORT.md that does not exist, and several of its figures have no raw output behind them or contradict provenance.json
findings.evidence: Line 91 cites `../REPORT.md`, but `ls docs/progress/evidence/anatomy-atlas/REPORT.md` returns 'No such file or directory'. Line 84 says FMA.csv has 104 723 classes, provenance.json:21 says 104698, and parsing the CSV gives 104721 rows and 104698 unique FMAIDs (wc -l is 104724). The figures 16 141 UBERON classes, 6 074 human classes, 930 meshes, 358 984 triangles and 93 female structures (lines 56, 63-64, 82) appear in no phase0 raw file, even though line 4 says every claim maps to a file in that folder. I re-derived each of these and they are correct, apart from the FMA count.
findings.fix: Add the missing REPORT.md or remove the reference. Save the command outputs for the counts in phase0. Correct the FMA count to 104 698 unique classes.

findings.title: The viewer's aria-label in the Mujer view does not say the body is the male reference model
findings.evidence: In female mode the label reads 'Modelo anatómico 3D, cuerpo en vista «Mujer»'. In male mode it says 'masculino de referencia'. A screen-reader user focusing the canvas is not told that the female view still shows the male body, unless they also reach the separate role=note paragraph.
findings.fix: Use 'cuerpo masculino de referencia sin genitales masculinos (vista «Mujer»)' or similar.

summary:
I found three major issues: Netter/Elsevier text is shipped and shown, machine-translated Spanish names appear without a label in most places, and the «Mujer» list leaves out the uterus. Three smaller issues concern the evidence trail and accessibility.

**Netter/Elsevier text is shipped.** 805 Netter index names with plate numbers are in public/anatomy-atlas-3d/catalog/ and shown under «En el índice de Netter». 8 of them are scraped page-header fragments of the book («Atlas de anatomía hum…»). netter-mapping/*.json commits all 3161 index names. Nothing records a rights check, and the credits do not mention Netter. This breaks the "no Netter text" requirement.

**Spanish labels.** `displayName()` shows the machine-translated name by default in the card title, search results, related structures, the female list and the viewer label, all without the «traducción automática sin revisar» label. Only the 'Nombre en castellano' row and the Spanish definition carry it.

**«Mujer» view.** The female list is built only from structures that sit under 'female reproductive system'. In UBERON the uterus sits under the sex-neutral 'internal genitalia', so the uterus, cervix, myometrium and uterine artery never make the list.

**Smaller issues:**
- DISCOVERY says the BodyParts3D credit comes from bodyparts3d-LICENSE_content.txt, but that file has a different credit ('Copyright 2008 …'). The shipped wording comes from line 4 of the BodyParts3D copy's README, which was not saved as evidence.
- DISCOVERY points to ../REPORT.md, which does not exist.
- The FMA class count disagrees between DISCOVERY (104 723) and provenance.json (104698). The CSV has 104721 rows and 104698 unique IDs.
- Several counts in DISCOVERY have no raw output in phase0, though I re-derived them and they are correct.
- In the «Mujer» view the viewer's screen-reader label does not say it is still the male body.

**Checks that passed:**
- **3D files:** all five GLBs carry the BodyParts3D CC-BY-SA 2.1 JP notice in asset.copyright. Together they hold 930 meshes and 358 984 triangles. Every mesh is a BodyParts3D STL (only skin and three hair sets are left out), and the parts manifest carries the same license.
- **License file:** public/anatomy-atlas-3d/models/LICENSE.txt credits the source, links the license, lists the changes and keeps the same license.
- **Z-Anatomy:** none of its files are shipped, so none of its non-commercial parts are either.
- **UBERON:** I checked the local uberon.obo (same SHA-256 as provenance.json) and the definitions are copied word for word (0 mismatches across 6322 entries). They are credited as CC-BY 3.0.
- **«Mujer» view:** it shows a visible notice that it is the male body, and hides only the 15 male genital parts.

I did not modify any repository files. The source downloads I used for comparison were already in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-mantra-core-health/0936bc81-5207-5906-b755-dffb86a17712/scratchpad/dl and /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-mantra-core-health/0936bc81-5207-5906-b755-dffb86a17712/scratchpad/onto/uberon.obo.

findings.title: The new organism and data client are missing from the docs, so check-doc-coverage reports two new findings
findings.evidence: `node scripts/check-doc-coverage.mjs` on the branch: '✗ check-doc-coverage — 65 hallazgo(s)', which includes 'organismo sin mencionar: app-anatomy-viewer (AnatomyViewer)' and 'servicio sin mencionar: AnatomyAtlasClient'. The same script on an origin/mockup export (git archive into the scratchpad) gives '63 hallazgo(s)', and neither line is there. The gate already failed on the base; the branch adds 2 more findings.
findings.fix: Mention AnatomyViewer in the organisms catalogue under docs/components/ and AnatomyAtlasClient in the data-access docs, so the count goes back to 63.

findings.title: The generated route list was not regenerated, so /glossary/anatomy-atlas is not covered by yarn pw:rutas
findings.evidence: `grep -n 'glossary/' docs/reports/generated/rutas.json` finds only '/glossary/:conceptId' (l.2476) and '/glossary/network' (l.2499). The new route is missing. playwright/support/salud-de-rutas.ts:52 builds the route-health sweep (carril-19, yarn pw:rutas) from that file, so the new route is never visited by it. `node scripts/audit-design-views.mjs --check` reports '2 salida(s) del auditor quedaron desactualizadas' both on the branch and on the origin/mockup export. The drift was already there; the branch makes it worse by adding a route nobody registered.
findings.fix: Run `yarn audit:vistas` (node scripts/audit-design-views.mjs) and commit the updated rutas.json and design-view-inventory.md.

summary:
I found no blocking regression for the existing consumers. The two problems I found are minor and both concern docs and generated route files. Verdict: PASS_WITH_ISSUES. This is not REGRESSION_VERIFIED, because some checks did not run (listed at the end).

What I checked, with evidence:

**1. Route order (src/app/app.routes.ts)**
- The order is anatomy-atlas (l.1037), then network (l.1046), then :conceptId (l.1061). The new route comes before :conceptId, so neither one hides the other.
- It has the same `seccionRolesGuard` as its sibling routes.
- I opened each page by typing the URL directly into the browser, against the production SSR build in dist/ (run with `node dist/mantra-core-health/server/server.mjs`):
  - logged in as the doctor (medica): /glossary/anatomy-atlas, /glossary/network and /glossary/91126f66-… (a term page, title 'Término del glosario', h1 'Densitometría ósea') all opened with no page errors;
  - not logged in: /glossary/anatomy-atlas sent me to /auth;
  - logged in as the patient (paciente) at 375 px: both /glossary/anatomy-atlas and /glossary sent me to /dashboard, the same access rule as before.
- The link `glosario-atlas-3d` on /glossary reaches /glossary/anatomy-atlas.
- The deep link ?structure=UBERON:0002107 opens the liver entry.
- The page is marked under 'Glosario' in the menu, and the breadcrumb reads 'Panel / Atención / Glosario'.

**2. Five viewports (375, 768, 1024, 1440, 1920)**
- The viewer reached `data-status="ready"` at every size, with no horizontal scroll (overflowX=0) and no console errors.

**3. CSP and the mock interceptor**
- src/server/security-headers.ts is not in the diff. The server sends the same CSP header for the HTML, the JSON files and the .glb models (`model/gltf-binary`).
- The .glb files contain no images or textures (only KHR_mesh_quantization), so they need no extra CSP permission (`blob:`).
- mock-backend.interceptor.ts was not changed, and it does not need to be: the regex at l.279 already lets through any path ending in a file extension, which covers /anatomy-atlas-3d/*.json and *.glb.

**4. Bundle and dependencies**
- three is not in main-*.js. It only appears in lazy chunks, and it is loaded only in the browser, after the first render.
- The initial bundle is 378.00 kB on the branch against 378.22 kB on the base (gzipped size reported by the build), with the same set of budget warnings. `check-bundle-budget` exits 0.
- package.json and yarn.lock pin three and @types/three at exactly 0.180.0, and node_modules has both installed at 0.180.0.
- The barrel export in organisms/index.ts only adds `export type` plus a component with no static import of three.

**5. Lint, typecheck and indexes**
- `eslint` on the changed files and `tsc -p tsconfig.app.json` / `tsc -p playwright/tsconfig.json` all pass.
- `generate-component-index.mjs --check`: '✓ al día (631)'.
- check-route-prefixes, check-client-prefixes and check-api-prefixes pass.
- check-css-tokens, check-tokens, check-usted and check-form-pages fail on both the branch and the base, with the same output.

**6. Scoped Vitest runs**
- app.routes, section-roles.guard, the atlas page, the atlas client and the viewer: 102/103 passed.
- navigation/** and glossary/**: 372/373 passed.
- mock fixtures, interceptor and tutorials: 113/114 passed.
- Each run has one failure, and I believe none are caused by this branch:
  - app.routes.spec l.253 (the my-account/identity/cases redirect);
  - access-tree.spec l.209 (the 'portada' entry);
  - fichas-estandar.spec, which fails with ENOENT because the sibling repo mantra-core-health-api is not on this machine.
- I did not re-run those three on the base. I ruled them out only because the code they test is not in the diff.

**Not verified, and why**
- `yarn pw:rutas` and `yarn pw:accesos`: `ng serve` was killed for running out of memory (exit 137, a ~4 GB memory limit in this sandbox). Also, pw:rutas would not visit the new route anyway (see the second finding).
- I used the build already in dist/, made at 01:44 from this branch, instead of building again.
- I did not test mutations; the atlas is read-only.

**Warning: another agent was changing the repo while I reviewed it.** HEAD moved from 757124f9 to d607403a, and 49 uncommitted changed files appeared, in the atlas page, the viewer, data/ and the catalog JSON. That commit and those changes leave the integration files alone: app.routes.ts, glossary.html, organisms/index.ts, package.json, yarn.lock, the interceptor and security-headers. However, my test, lint and browser results for the atlas page and the viewer were taken on files that were changing at the same time. They need to be re-run once that work is committed. I did not modify any file in the repo.
